children: Kuwait’s government issued a decree on Tuesday allowing it to borrow from its more than $1 trillion sovereign wealth fund, ending a decades-old ban and helping support the state treasury as lower oil revenues and disruptions to shipping on the Strait of Hormuz weigh on public finances.

Under the new Amiri decree, the government may borrow from the Future Generations Fund (FGF), which is managed by the Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA). The borrowings will support the General Reserve Fund (GRF), which finances the state budget.

The decree sets out several conditions, including that the amount, purpose, interest rate, tenor and repayment schedule of any loan must be specified in advance. Repayment of the loan must be prioritised, and the total borrowing amount, which cannot be written off except by law, must not exceed 10% of the value of the FGF's assets.

Kuwait, the fifth-largest oil producer in OPEC, has been among the Gulf's hardest-hit oil exporters as the conflict has disrupted export shipments through the Strait. Kuwait’s deficit for the just ended fiscal 2025-26 widened to KWD 7.1 billion ($23 billion), or 15% of the GDP from KWD 1.1 billion in the previous year.
EFG Hermes views the move as positive for the Kuwaiti government, as it provides an additional financing option.

"With approximately $1 trillion in assets under management at the FGF, the new law provides a total space of approximately $100 billion of total borrowing, a significant 63% of GDP. In that respect, the amended law provides the government with a sizeable second avenue to finance its fiscal deficit having passed the public debt law in 2025," said Mohamed Abu Basha, lead economist at EFG Hermes.
In the global debt markets, the sovereign, which is rated AA- and A1 by Fitch Ratings and Moody’s, raised $6 billion in a triple tranche bond issuance in July.
(Writing by Brinda Darasha; editing by Seban Scaria)

title: Kuwait issues decree allowing government to borrow from wealth fund
